subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw define an owner-confirmed responsibility lifecycle in core/plugin APIs now, keep this as a coordinating umbrella while splitting implementation into narrower trust/provenance issues, or route external responsibility-chain integration outside core?
rationale: The requested lifecycle crosses persistent memory, reusable evidence, action approvals, plugin/skill governance, UI auditability, and public config, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Keep Umbrella, Split Implementation
options.body: Keep this issue open as the coordinating security design item, then implement only maintainer-approved narrow contracts for memory state, hook/API exposure, and audit UI.

options.title: Close Into Narrow Existing Issues
options.body: Treat the remaining work as covered by narrower memory provenance, source-tracking, tainting, and sub-agent review issues and use those as the canonical implementation path.

options.title: External Plugin/Interop First
options.body: Require SCBKR/UMP-style responsibility chains to prove out as a plugin or external interop layer before adding core lifecycle state.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella, Split Implementation
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the coordinating security design item, then implement only maintainer-approved narrow contracts for memory state, hook/API exposure, and audit UI.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail ties Peter Steinberger to the memory host SDK, memory-core seams, external-content hardening, and approval infrastructure this decision would coordinate.
